title.value: We offer assistance with
Five South Carolina Rules That Decide When You Get Paid

paragraph.value: South Carolina’s payment rules live in two places, the state insurance code and Healthy Connections policy. These are the five our team checks on every claim:

settings.title_text: Prompt Pay: 20 Business Days Electronic, 40 Paper

paragraph.value: Under S.C. Code § 38-59-230, an insurance company has 20 working days to pay or deny the electronic claim. If the insurer takes more time, they owe you interest on the money. It works the same way as a late load payment carries interest. We help submit accurate claims and log the receipt date so we can bill the interest if the commercial payer does not pay within the time limit.

The deadline of the 20 business days applies to a “clean claim.” The definition of a clean claim contains the time as well. If the insurer receives the claim within 120 working days of the day the patient was seen, the claim is clean. If the claim is sent on the day 121, it is not clean and the 20-day deadline never starts.

settings.title_text: Billing Services May Not Downgrade Your Claims to Paper

paragraph.value: Some clearinghouses and billing companies used to print the electronic claim, print it out, and mail it. It started with a 40-day clock instead of a 20-day clock. South Carolina made this illegal and called it an unfair trade practice. We keep the claims electronic all the way to comply with the state rules.

settings.title_text: Dual-Eligible, Waiver and Nursing-Facility Members Are in Managed Care

paragraph.value: Healthy Connections members who have Medicare as well, members in home- and community-based waiver programs, and nursing-facility residents aged 18 and over are now enrolled in managed care plans for their medical services. The waiver services themselves and the nursing-facility stay in fee-for-service, so one patient can have two payers. Plans must honor a newly enrolled member’s existing prior authorizations for 180 days at fee-for-service rates, even out of network. We re-verify each affected patient’s plan and track that window so the claim goes where it will be paid.

Healthy Connections Prime, the plan that combined Medicare and Medicaid for dual-eligible members, no longer exists. What do those members carry now? They carry a Dual Special Needs Plan or standard Medicare on one side and a Healthy Connections managed care plan on the other, which means two payers, two portals and two claims for one visit. We split and route each claim to the correct side to ensure accuracy.

settings.title_text: Insurers Have 18 Months to Take a Payment Back

paragraph.value: Under S.C. Code § 38-59-250, a commercial insurer may not start recovering an overpayment more than eighteen months after the provider received it, and must give thirty business days’ written notice before offsetting it against other claims. The limit does not apply where the insurer reasonably suspects fraud, to self-insured plans, or to government programs. We log the payment date on every commercial claim so a late recoupment can be challenged on the date alone.

settings.title_text: The Department of Insurance Enforces the Clock

paragraph.value: The prompt-pay article gives providers no right to sue; § 38-59-270 puts enforcement with the South Carolina Department of Insurance. When a fully insured plan runs past the deadline and does not pay interest, the route is a complaint to the Department, with the claim’s receipt date and the remittance attached. We keep both on file for every commercial claim so the complaint can be built without a search.

title.value: One Medicaid Program, Two Tracks: Fee-for-Service vs Managed Care

paragraph.value: Healthy Connections pays a claim in one of the two ways. But what determines which way? It depends on the service and the member, not on the practice. Our experts track the claim from the beginning which is the time when eligibility is determined. So, every claim goes to the payer that will pay it.
Which track pays the claim?

settings.description_text: Who pays: SCDHHS, from the state Medicaid budget
At what rate: the state fee schedule
Where the claim goes: to SCDHHS

title.value: Plan track

settings.description_text: Who pays: the member’s managed care plan

title.value: Track checked before the claim is built

paragraph.value: The claim is checked by our team before it is created, not after it comes back denied. The member’s plan is confirmed at eligibility on every date of service.

title.value: South Carolina Medical Billing Services for Every Payer

paragraph.value: Our billers and coders work the four payer types that fill a South Carolina practice’s A/R. We bill:

title.value: Healthy Connections Managed Care Plans

paragraph.value: Most Medicaid patients have one of five plans: Absolute Total Care, Healthy Blue, Humana Healthy Horizons, Molina or Select Health. Each plan is different due to a different portal, different prior authorization rules, and different time windows for appeals. As a medical billing company in South Carolina, we confirm the member’s plan on every date the services are offered because we take care of the carve-in changes.

title.value: BlueCross BlueShield of South Carolina

paragraph.value: Most commercial claims a practice based in South Carolina are sent to the BCBSSC. It runs on the 20-day prompt-pay clock, so we make sure that claim falls under the deadline before it goes out. We bill the interest when a clean claim is late.

title.value: TRICARE

paragraph.value: Fort Jackson, Shaw Air Force Base, Joint Base Charleston and Parris Island put military families in waiting rooms from Columbia to the Lowcountry. TRICARE claims run through the regional contractor’s referral and authorization rules, not the base’s, and they fail for reasons commercial claims never do. Medical practices that outsource medical billing in South Carolina to us get a team that already knows those rules.

title.value: Medicare

paragraph.value: South Carolina’s Part A and Part B claims are paid by Palmetto GBA, the Jurisdiction M contractor headquartered in Columbia. We code to Palmetto’s local coverage determinations and keep track of the prior authorizations. For documentation requests, we answer from the record. So, Medicare claims do not get delayed due to any discrepancies in the record.

title.value: Workers’ Compensation

paragraph.value: Work-injury claims in South Carolina are paid under the Workers’ Compensation Commission’s medical fee schedule, not under the practice’s commercial contracts, and they go to the employer’s carrier with the claim number, not to the patient’s health plan. We bill them from the Commission’s schedule and keep them out of the commercial A/R so they are not worked against the wrong rules.
Medicaid Compliance

title.value: Healthy Connections Compliance Rules We Build Into Every Claim

paragraph.value: South Carolina Medicaid has its own deadlines and record rules, separate from the state insurance code. These four are in SCDHHS’s Provider Administrative and Billing Guide, and each one is a denial or a recovery if it is missed.
Source: SCDHHS Provider Administrative and Billing Guide, Section 1
Timely filing

title.value: One Year to File

paragraph.value: A Healthy Connections claim is considered for payment only if it is received and entered within one year of the date of service, or the discharge date for hospital claims. Medicare cost-sharing claims get two years from the date of service or six months from the Medicare payment date, whichever is later. We work the one-year date from the day the claim is created, not from the first denial.
Enrollment

title.value: Enrolled With SCDHHS, Not Just the Plan

paragraph.value: A provider who contracts with one or more Healthy Connections managed care plans must also be enrolled with SCDHHS. Plan credentialing alone does not make a provider a South Carolina Medicaid provider, and claims from an un-enrolled provider fail at the state level no matter which plan the member is in. We check SCDHHS enrollment before the first managed care claim goes out.
Records

title.value: Four Years of Records

paragraph.value: Medicaid providers must keep fiscal and health records for a minimum of four years after the last payment; hospitals and nursing facilities keep them for six. When SCDHHS Program Integrity asks for a record and it is not produced, the payment can be recovered and the provider sanctioned. We keep the claim, the remittance and the supporting documentation together for the full retention period.
Program Integrity

title.value: Program Integrity Can Recover, Suspend and Exclude

paragraph.value: SCDHHS Program Integrity exists to find waste, fraud and abuse in Medicaid funds, and the Provider Guide bars every form of kickback and self-referral. A records request from Program Integrity is answered from the record on time, because the alternative is recovery of the payment and, in the worst case, exclusion from the program.

title.value: Is every claim on the right South Carolina clock?

paragraph.value: We check your recent claims against the 20-business-day prompt-pay window, the 120-day clean-claim limit and each Healthy Connections plan’s rules, and show you where payment is stalling. The review is free and the findings are yours to keep.

title.value: Step-by-Step Billing Process Breakdown

paragraph.value: The process breakdown shows how we handle the medical claims for practices based in South Carolina. For Medicare claims, we check the claims against the coverage policies of Palmetto GBA. The Medicaid claims are analyzed against the managed care plan of the member. For commercial plans, we check it against the contract. The steps mentioned below are what medical practices in South Carolina see from the outside.

settings.description_text: Before the patient’s visit, our team verifies eligibility to reduce the chances of claim rejections. For Healthy Connections, we confirm which plan among the five managed care plans the patient is enrolled with. It is not necessary that the plan on the card is going to pay for the rendered services. If the claim is sent to the wrong payer, it surely leads to a claim denial.

Our medical coders are adept at what they do and they match the documentation to the codes. They check the Medicare claims whether these claims align with the Palmetto GBA’s local coverage determinations before submitting to the payer.

Electronic claims are submitted electronically to Palmetto GBA, managed care plans, and the commercial payers by our team. The prompt-pay clock begins for the electronic claims sent to the commercial payers in South Carolina.

Our team posts payment from every payer against the claim. It is done line by line, so you see what was paid and what was adjusted. What the payer still owes and what the patient needs to pay, everything is mentioned.

Claim denials are resubmitted by our team after corrections or our team of denial management experts appeal within the deadline of the payer. Aging accounts receivable is worked by our team until we help South Carolina practices get accurately paid.

You get reports that have all the details about the claims and payments. The reports give you an idea about the payers that delay payments, which claims get denied the most, and which areas need improvement.

title.value: AAPC and AHIMA Coders for South Carolina Claims

paragraph.value: The payers in South Carolina pay on the codes mentioned on the medical claim and coding accuracy is essential to get complete payments. Our medical coders hold AAPC or AHIMA credentials and work with CPT, ICD-10-CM and HCPCS daily.

Certified coders identify errors that lead to denials in South Carolina, like a procedure code that invites an NCCI edit at Palmetto, a diagnosis that does not go with the medical necessity under a local coverage determination, or a modifier that does not align with the place of service. Every code is used correctly before the claims leave our team instead of reworking the denials.
What certified coding gives a South Carolina practice:

Coding matched to each payer’s level of specificity, from Medicaid managed care to TRICARE
Working knowledge of CPT, ICD-10-CM and HCPCS, including Palmetto GBA’s local coverage rules
Fewer coding denials and less revenue written off
Internal audits that keep the coding team’s accuracy measured, not assumed

paragraph.value: Palmetto GBA, under Jurisdiction M, processes Part A and Part B claims for South Carolina, North Carolina, Virginia and West Virginia. It is headquartered in Columbia. Its local coverage determinations and prior authorization programs are what a South Carolina Medicare claim is judged against, so coding to Palmetto’s rules is part of our standard workflow.

Managed care plans used by Healthy Connections are Absolute Total Care, Healthy Blue, Humana Healthy Horizons, Molina or Select Health (First Choice). Every managed care plan has its own portal, prior authorization requirements and time windows for appeal. We confirm the member’s plan on the date of service because the plan at the time of intake is not always the one that is going to pay.

Two things. SCDHHS moved dual-eligible members, waiver members and nursing-facility residents aged 18 and over into managed care plans for their medical services, while waiver and nursing-facility services stayed fee-for-service; plans must honor existing prior authorizations for 180 days. On the same day, Healthy Connections Prime, the state’s Medicare-Medicaid plan, ended, and its members moved to a Dual Special Needs Plan or a standard Medicare plan alongside their Medicaid plan.

Under S.C. Code § 38-59-230, an insurer must pay or deny a clean electronic claim within 20 business days and a paper claim within 40. Interest runs on late payment under § 38-59-240. The rule applies to fully insured commercial plans; Medicare, Medicaid and self-funded employer plans are outside it. We submit electronically and track the receipt date so the clock is on your side.

One year from the date of service, or from discharge for hospital claims; the claim has to be received and entered by then, not just sent. Commercial claims run on the contract’s timely filing limit, which is often shorter, and the state’s prompt-pay protection only applies to a claim received within 120 business days.

The pricing of the medical billing services is a percentage of collections. So, when you get paid, we get paid. There are no setup fees and the percentage depends on specialty, volume of the claims, payer mix. This is what we determine after a short review of your current billing.
